citation.title: Comparison of experimental and theoretical fast ion slowing-down times in DIII-D
citation.authors: W.W. Heidbrink, Jinchoon Kim, R.J. Groebner

topic: Classical slowing-down of short deuterium beam pulses, inferred from the decay of d(d,n)3He neutron emission in DIII-D. The paper also uses these pulses for relative central deuterium density estimates.
own_question: The paper asks whether beam-ion deceleration agrees with Sivukhin classical Coulomb drag.
actual_method_and_evidence: Approximately 2 ms pulses of 74 keV D0 were injected into steady deuterium plasmas. Neutron decay times were compared with a test-particle calculation. The calculation used fitted Te and ne profiles and included H, D and C species. The authors report that the measured-to-theory decay-time ratio was about 0.85 ± 0.15, with stated agreement to within about 30%. The analysis was offline. It did not involve CES impurity Ti, BES/ECEI, nowcasting or a validation split.
input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not applicable. Neutron detection had sub-0.1 ms resolution. The analysis was retrospective and is unrelated to online estimation of CES reports.
validation_if_relevant: The paper compares experiment with theory across a set of discharges. It has no held-out data and no causal evaluation.
forbidden_inferences: Do not cite this paper as evidence about carbon-impurity CES temperature or main-ion Ti measurement.
Do not cite it as prior work on causal nowcasting or on BES/ECEI fusion.
Do not cite it for KSTAR or pedestal-top relevance.
Do not treat its central nd estimate as an ion-temperature diagnostic.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Exclude. The paper only addresses beam-ion slowing-down physics and neutron diagnostics. Classical ion-electron coupling is only tangential background, and our study does not require it.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
